neuro-landscape · Oct 2026 · 02/24
// 01 · the question
Where can computational neuroscience skills build a career outside academia? Which of those bets will still exist in five years?
who is there
established labs, startups, university spin-offs
what runs hot
excitement against money
what lasts
longevity, health impact, economic and ecological sustainability
// 02 · method
How the map was built
The brief
· About 100 organisations, worldwide with a Europe zoom, as of October 2026
· Three tiers: big companies’ neuro programmes, startups, university spin-offs
· My four starting trends; four more added only where the data showed them
· In scope: anything that measures, decodes, stimulates or models brain or behaviour, or computes like a brain
The process
1 One search per area, plus one for gaps (China, EEG/MEG makers, Marseille): 152 candidates
2 Duplicates merged, thin or off-topic ones dropped: 119 kept
3 35 headline facts re-checked at the source: 24 right, 11 fixed, 0 wrong
4 Each organisation scored 1–5 on five separate dimensions, with a written reason
No hierarchy in the scores. Ecological is scored only for the 27 organisations where energy or compute matters.
Result: 119 organisations, 87 investment rounds, 122 news items from 2025–26, each with a source. Limits: only announced money; scores are judgement, not measurement; Europe over-represented on purpose.

// 09 · who pays
Before we zoom in: who actually pays
Paying their way
Ceribell $89.1M revenue in 2025, +36%
NeuroPace ~$100M revenue guided for 2026
Medtronic adaptive DBS approved; ~$539M a quarter in neuromodulation
Smart Eye sales +53% on EU rules
Brainomix AI in routine stroke care
g.tec, Noldus decades of self-funded instrument sales
Money raised, then closed or sold
VERSES AI stopped all AI work (Jun 2026)
Rain AI collapsed; OpenAI bought patents (2026)
Kintsugi closed after ~$30M (Feb 2026)
Move AI assets sold for £525k (Oct 2026)
Mindstrong closed after ~$160M (2023)
Neuronetics going-concern doubt; Tobii strained liquidity; MindMaze rescue financing (2026)
Before joining a startup, ask: how many months of runway, what is the path to approval, who pays? · 10/24
// 10 · zoom 1 of 5
BCI & wearables: the money magnet
Implants race to approval
Neuralink $650M, Synchron $200M, Precision $250M (FDA-cleared for up to 30 days), Science Corp $230M.
Non-surgical bets
Merge Labs ~$250M with OpenAI, Nudge $100M: ultrasound instead of surgery.
China and wearables
Neuracle reports China’s first approved implanted BCI. Meta’s EMG wristband is on sale.
roles: neural decoding · neural data science · clinical research · neuroengineering · 11/24
// 11 · case study · BCI & wearables
Synchron: a brain implant without open-skull surgery
An electrode array threaded through a blood vessel next to the motor cortex lets people with paralysis control phones and computers.
› $345M raised, including a $200M Series D (Nov 2025)
› First BCI built into Apple’s devices; trains a brain model with NVIDIA
› Next step: the pivotal trial needed for approval

// 12 · zoom 2 of 5
Neural foundation models: research is exploding
Big labs publish openly
Meta FAIR in Paris: an open fMRI model (TRIBE v2); typing decoded from MEG at ~61% of words.
Startups bet on EEG
Hemispheric $52M, Sabi $50M, Piramidal with Cleveland Clinic for intensive-care EEG.
The gap is validation
We found no independent test behind any startup’s accuracy claim.
roles: research scientist · ML on brain signals · datasets and evaluation · 13/24
// 13 · case study · neural foundation models
Meta FAIR Brain & AI: industry neuroscience in Paris
A research team building open AI models of how the brain processes language, images and sound.
› TRIBE v2 predicts fMRI responses to video, audio and text, released openly (Mar 2026)
› Brain2Qwerty v2 decodes typed sentences from MEG at ~61% of words (preprint)
› Co-funds an open brain-data project with Fondation Rothschild in Paris

// 14 · zoom 3 of 5
Behaviour & motion data: robots are the buyer
Robots buy human motion
People film everyday tasks for robot training: Mecka $60M (Sequoia), Ropedia $22M, Human Archive $8M.
Old models struggle
Move AI sold for £525k; phone-based mood apps Kintsugi and Mindstrong closed.
Rules draw the lines
EU AI Act bans emotion reading at work and school; gait, voice and gaze are barely protected.
roles: behavioural scientist · data design · ML for pose and video · 15/24
// 15 · case study · behaviour & motion data
Mecka: selling human motion to robot makers
Pays people to film everyday tasks from a head-mounted camera; robot companies train on the footage.
› $8M seed (2025), then a $60M Series B led by Sequoia (Oct 2026)
› Part of a wave: Ropedia $22M, Human Archive $8M
› Contrast: Move AI, a motion-capture startup, sold its assets for £525k

Consciousness & AI: philanthropy, not venture
No venture money
Funding is philanthropic: Astera Neuro has $600M+ over ten years.
Labs and non-profits
Anthropic’s model-welfare team, Eleos AI, PRISM in the UK.
The clinic is concrete

roles: research scientist (theory, evaluation) · clinical neurophysiology · 17/24
// 17 · case study · consciousness & AI
Intrinsic Powers: measuring consciousness at the bedside
Founded by Christof Koch, Marcello Massimini and Giulio Tononi: a TMS-EEG test to detect hidden consciousness in unresponsive patients.
› Runs on a $0.5M NIH seed grant
› Struggles to attract venture investors despite a large clinical need
› Contrast: VERSES, built on active inference, stopped all AI work (Jun 2026)

// 18 · zoom 5 of 5
The quiet four: where most of the revenue is
Neuromodulation
Medtronic’s adaptive deep brain stimulation and Flow’s home headset for depression are approved.
Digital psychiatry
Ceribell’s EEG with AI made $89M in 2025. Alto’s EEG-biomarker trial missed.
Neuromorphic
Chips are in production but cash is thin; Rain AI collapsed.
NeuroAI
Liquid AI ($288M) now sells efficient AI models; VERSES stopped.
roles: clinical and translational scientist · signal processing · regulated data · 19/24
// 19 · case study · neuromodulation
ONWARD Medical: from an EPFL lab to revenue
Spinal-cord stimulation that restores arm, hand and leg movement after spinal cord injury.
› External system cleared and selling: €2.0M revenue in Q1 2026, 100+ clinics
› Implant in a pivotal trial; €40M+ raised in 2026, cash into 2028
› Listed on Euronext; built on EPFL / NeuroRestore research

// 22 · takeaways
Five things to take home
01 The money is in BCI; the revenue is in the clinic. 
02 Neural foundation models are the closest match to our training, and validation is the scarce skill.
03 Know who pays: robotics buys behaviour data; philanthropy funds consciousness research.
04 Two in three startups and spin-offs have no proven business
05 PIs: open code and data, industry co-supervision, room for production work collaboration, more?
